rendered: The review does not say that. It says DRX materials are generally made at gram scale by energy-intensive methods: "DRX materials are generally synthesized in gram-scale"[1] "quantities using energy-intensive mechanochemical and solid-state methods"[2]. It then argues that DRX synthesis needs more scalable routes before its commercial viability can be judged: "scalable routes (e.g., coprecipitation) are needed to better assess[3]" their commercial viability. Coprecipitation is presented as a proven, scalable route for other cathodes. The review says "[4]" and that it "[5]" high-performance layered cathodes, such as the NFA materials scaled to kilogram levels by coprecipitation. So coprecipitation is cited as the scalable option DRX cathodes still lack, not as a method already used for them.
